newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S'pore HSFO seen off on diminishing Chinese demand.
newsitem.headline: S'pore HSFO seen off on diminishing Chinese demand.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were seen steady to soft on Tuesday with some traders saying that fundamentals are under pressure as demand from China eases.
"If February supplies from South Korea and Mideast were unchanged from January, thin demand from China during the festive China Lunar new Year holidays would cause prices to ease," a trader said.
"Activities in the Chinese market would come to a halt with the Chinese New Year lasting more than half a month as power companies and industries would be close," he said.
High sulphur 180-cst fuel oil levels were assessed at $123/$125 per tonne on Monday.
January swaps edged up slightly with January quoted at $121.25/$122.25 per tonne, up 50 cents from Monday.
The local trader seen active last week is unlikley to move any cargoes today, traders said.
"A couple of majors should be offering some barrels but I think buying interest would be thin," said another trader.
Late Tuesday, an offer was seen at $124.75 per tonne for late January loading supplies against a bid at $122.
